subject: Discrepancy: GCP hourly usage window shift impacting June marketplace invoices
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-cloud.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: marketplace-finance@acme-cloud.com
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2029 12:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: June invoice mismatch — possible hourly bucket shift

Jordan,

We pulled our marketplace bill for June and are seeing ~€48k of usage that landed on two different invoice lines when compared to the daily usage export we pulled from GCP. The big signal is that a chunk of hourly usage around 00:00 UTC on June 10-11 appears to be split between two service days on your invoice vs our internal export. That split is causing VAT to be allocated across two invoice entities in our ledger and has triggered a withheld payout on our side while we reconcile.

I've attached a small CSV extract (acme_gcp_billing_export_202906.csv) showing the two buckets and the invoice PDF (invoice_ACME-202906.pdf) for reference — you can see the same hourly lines mapped differently. Can you confirm how Redwood pairs hourly GCP usage to marketplace invoice lines? Any immediate thoughts on timezone or daylight-savings related shifts?

We need an answer by EOD Thursday (our local CET) to unfreeze the payout for June. Happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Billing — Acme Cloud
Acme Cloud Marketplace

Attachments: acme_gcp_billing_export_202906.csv, invoice_ACME-202906.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2029 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: June invoice mismatch — possible hourly bucket shift

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear extract and the PDF. We see the same lines in the export you attached. I'm looped in from our marketplace billing & finance teams to triage. Initial ask: can you confirm the timezone that your ledger uses for invoice pairing (UTC vs CET) and whether you applied any manual proration rules?

Marissa / Jonas — can you take point on quick triage here? Specifically we should: 1) verify our hourly-to-invoice mapping logic for June (any DST edges), 2) produce a pairing CSV that maps each GCP hourly row -> Redwood invoice line, and 3) flag any cases where we changed the day boundary for aggregation. Hannah — heads up since they've flagged a withheld payout until we can reconcile VAT allocation.

I'll start a Jira ticket and drop the BigQuery query results into the ticket. Liam, I'll follow up with a proposed 30-minute window for Thursday CET.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Manager, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Related: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/BILL-328
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jun 2029 09:14:00 +0100
Subject: Re: June invoice mismatch — possible hourly bucket shift

Thanks Jordan — dug into this this morning. Summary of preliminary findings: 

- Root cause candidate: June 10-11 overlaps with a config change in our ingestion pipeline where we switched a legacy hourly aggregation job from rounding at 23:59:59 UTC to a calendar-day window anchored to account-local timezone (we rolled this change for a subset of sellers to improve per-tenant reporting). That change inadvertently affected accounts with GMT+1/CET clocks, causing an apparent split when compared to a pure-UTC export.

- Impact: ~€48,120 tied to 18 hourly buckets (06:00–01:00 UTC pairs) mapped to different invoice lines in our generated PDF vs the raw export. No tokens were double-billed; this is an aggregation/pairing mismatch.

- VAT implication: because the split moved part of the usage into a different invoice entity (EU reseller vs UK reseller in our setup), VAT was allocated differently and triggered Acme's payout hold.

Action items I'm taking now:
1) Produce the hour-to-invoice pairing matrix and attach as reconciliation_matrix_202906.xlsx (ETA today EOD CET).
2) Re-run the June aggregator for affected sellers in a dry-run mode and produce a delta report.
3) Add a migration rollback if the dry-run indicates re-anchoring to UTC is required for these sellers.

Jonas — can you validate the DB snapshot (billing.hours_agg_20290610) and confirm whether the pipeline toggle was on for Acme's tenant id (acme-tenant-018)?

Liam — sorry for the disruption. We'll prioritize the pairing matrix and a concise note you can push to your finance team for releasing the hold today if the numbers check out.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Marketplace Billing Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments pending: reconciliation_matrix_202906.xlsx
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jun 2029 11:26:00 +0100
Subject: Re: June invoice mismatch — possible hourly bucket shift

Folks — quick finance note from our side: Acme's withheld payout is for the EU VAT allocation difference (approx €48k). For us to approve a release we need: 1) hour->invoice pairing CSV, 2) confirmation that there is no change to net revenue recognized (i.e., no double-counting), and 3) an updated invoice PDF if we re-anchor aggregation. If the pairing matrix proves it's purely a grouping mismatch and net is unchanged, we can approve a one-off payout release and then run a cleanup for July's invoice schedule.

Please include a short note explaining remediation steps (rollback vs config fix) and whether we need to issue a corrected invoice vs internal memo.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Finance, Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2029 16:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: June invoice mismatch — possible hourly bucket shift

Liam — attaching the requested reconciliation artifacts and next steps. Per Marissa's work this morning we've attached: 

- reconciliation_matrix_202906.xlsx (full hour -> Redwood invoice line pairing)
- acme_gcp_billing_export_202906.csv (your extract + normalized keys)
- short remediation summary: "For affected sellers we will re-anchor June hourly aggregation to UTC (dry-run shows mapping that aligns with Acme's UTC export). No net revenue change. We will: 1) release a one-off payout to Acme for €48,120, 2) issue an internal memo for VAT allocation reconciliation, and 3) apply a config fix to prevent tenant-anchored aggregation for marketplace sellers unless explicitly requested. ETA: payout release within 24 hours upon your confirmation to unfreeze."

I've opened BILL-328 and attached the BigQuery export in the ticket. Marissa/Jonas — please confirm the dry-run outputs by EOD so Hannah can approve the payment release. Liam — if that works for you please reply with a short confirm and we'll instruct finance to push the payout. Otherwise we can take the 30 min slot Friday 08:30 CET to walk through the spreadsheet.

Thanks and sorry again for the churn — appreciate the fast loop here.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Manager, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
